scenario: AITA for not giving my wife what she wants to eat? | I will try to keep this as concise as possible. My wife and I have been together for going on 27 years. We met at a pretty low point in both of our lives, coming from broken homes and an unhealthy dependency on food. We both probably weighed around 300lbs, and though our weight has fluctuated over the years we both currently sit at around 350lbs and 450lbs respectively, with her being the latter. I cook all the food that we eat as my wife is unable to be on her feet long enough to make meals. I am completely okay with this, as I’ve really been able to hone in on my cooking skills over the years and can essentially throw down in the kitchen. When my oldest daughter told us she was pregnant a few months back, it really made me reevaluate our lifestyle choices. I wanna be able to run around with my grandkids, but I can’t do that in my current situation. Over the course of several months I’ve been looking into healthier alternatives of our favorite foods and trying to exercise more, slowly implementing both into our lives and my wife was initially on board. More recently she’s stopped wanting to workout with me which I respected, but I’ve continued to cook healthier meals and she no longer wants to eat them. I’ve stopped buying junk and with a suspended license she can’t drive to get fast food, so I assumed she would just eat what I made like she always has. She feels like I’m forcing a lifestyle into her that she never agreed to, but I’m not pushing her to eat what I’ve made or workout. I suggested she could learn to cook what she wants and I would even help her, but I won’t continue to cook foods I no longer want to eat. Does this make me TA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being a toxic asshole (TA) in this situation with my wife. Let me start by understanding the context. We've been together for almost 27 years, which is a long time. We both came from broken homes and had an unhealthy relationship with food, which led us to be overweight. Currently, I weigh around 350 lbs and she's at 450 lbs. I cook all the food because she can't stand for long enough to prepare meals, and I'm okay with that because I've developed good cooking skills over the years. Recently, when our oldest daughter told us she was pregnant, it made me want to change our lifestyle so I can be more active with my grandkids. I started looking into healthier alternatives of our favorite foods and tried to exercise more. Initially, my wife was on board with these changes. However, lately she's stopped wanting to work out with me, which I respect. I continued cooking healthier meals, but she no longer wants to eat them. I stopped buying junk food, and since she has a suspended license, she can't drive to get fast food. I assumed she would eat what I made, like she always has. But she feels like I'm forcing a lifestyle change on her that she never agreed to. I'm not pushing her to eat what I've made or to work out. I suggested she could learn to cook what she wants, and I'd even help her, but I won't continue to cook foods I no longer want to eat. Now, the question is: Does this make me a toxic asshole? I need to think about what defines a toxic asshole in this context. From what I understand, a toxic asshole is someone who is controlling, disrespectful, or manipulative in a relationship. So, I need to evaluate my actions and see if they fit into any of these categories. First, I started making healthier meals because I want to improve our lifestyle, especially for the sake of our future with grandkids. That seems like a positive intention. I also respected her decision to stop working out with me, which shows consideration for her feelings and boundaries. I didn't push her to eat the healthier meals; instead, I suggested she could learn to cook what she wants, offering help. That seems like a collaborative approach rather than a controlling one. However, she feels like I'm forcing a lifestyle change on her. Maybe my approach, while well-intentioned, came across as imposing. I assumed she would eat what I made, but she's expressing that she doesn't want to. That could indicate a lack of communication or understanding on my part. I need to consider her feelings and preferences more carefully. Also, by stopping the purchase of junk food and limiting her access to fast food, I might be indirectly controlling her food choices. While I have the right to choose what I eat and what I cook, it's important to respect her autonomy in making her own food choices. If she wants to eat differently, she should have the freedom to do so, even if it means she needs to prepare her own meals or find alternative ways to get the food she wants. In summary, while my intentions are positive, my actions might be coming across as controlling or disrespectful to her autonomy. To avoid being a toxic asshole, I should focus on open communication, respect her boundaries, and find a balanced approach where both of our needs and preferences are considered.
